en: The Sūtra on the Rishi Kāśyapa Teaching a Woman Medicine,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order,
Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, Dharma-bhadra, by imperial decree.
At that time, the Ṛṣi Jīvaka suddenly had this thought:
"The bodies of all sentient beings in the world are born from women.
From the initial conception until the ten months are complete, or even when the pregnancy is extended to twelve months, it is only then that they give birth."
"Perhaps in the interim he may fall ill; while suffering from that illness, he will experience extreme pain.
I shall now employ skillful means to inquire of my teacher, receive prescriptions and medicines, and provide him with medical treatment."
Having formed this thought, he immediately went to the seer Kāśyapa, his teacher, and after performing the rites of a disciple toward a master, he asked:
"Master Kāśyapa is one of great wisdom; I now wish to ask a question, and I pray that you will grant me your attention."
The seer Kāśyapa said,
"Ask whatever you wish.
Then the seer Jīvaka addressed him, saying:
"A woman’s pregnancy lasts for ten months or twelve months, and only when the days are complete does she give birth.
Why is it that during the interim there may be various ailments, causing the fetus to move restlessly within the womb, or even resulting in injury, leading to immeasurable suffering?"
"My teacher possesses great wisdom; I pray that he will proclaim for me the prescriptions and medicines to cure such suffering of illness.
Having asked this, he remained there listening and receiving the teaching.
At that time, the seer Kāśyapa addressed the seer Jīvaka, saying:
"If a woman becomes pregnant but does not know how to protect herself, she will cause the fetus to become unstable.
I shall now briefly explain for you the medicines for protection according to the months."

If the fetus of a pregnant woman is unstable during the first month, one should take sandalwood, lotus flowers, and blue utpala flowers, grind them together with water, then add milk and sugar to boil as a decoction. By drinking this medicine while it is warm, the woman who has recently conceived will be free from all harm and affliction and attain peace and happiness.
Furthermore, he addressed the seer Jīvaka, saying:

"If a woman’s fetus is unstable during the second month of pregnancy, one should employ the following medicines: blue utpala flowers, the roots of kumuda flowers, the kernels of lotus seeds, and kaśeruka."
Take equal parts of the various medicinal ingredients, pound and sift them into a powder, and decoct them with breast milk. Once it has cooled, administer it.
This medicine will prevent damage to the fetus, cause pain to cease, and ensure peace and security day and night.

"Furthermore, if a woman’s fetus becomes unstable during the third month of pregnancy, one should take equal parts of *kākoḍumbara* medicine, *kṣīrakākolī* medicine, and the roots of *śatapuṣpā*, etc., and grind them with water until they are extremely fine. Then, add milk and boil them together until cooked; subsequently, add candied sugar and honey, mix them well, and administer while cold."
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; if there is a patient who takes it, they will find peace and comfort.

Furthermore, for a woman whose fetus becomes unstable during the fourth month of pregnancy, one should take equal parts of the roots, branches, and leaves of *kaṇṭakārikā*, along with the flowers and stalks of the *utpala*. These should be mixed with water and ground until extremely fine, then boiled together with milk until cooked. Once cooled, it should be administered.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; when the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, if a pregnant woman experiences instability in the womb during the fifth month, one should take equal parts of the root of the bottle gourd (*alābu*) and the blue lotus (*utpala*), grind and sift them until fine. Then, add grape juice, breast milk, and cow’s milk to boil together; once cooled, it should be consumed.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; when the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, for a woman whose fetus becomes unstable during the sixth month of pregnancy, one should take equal parts of the drugs *cīrā*, *sumanā-karavīra*, and *sakṛdvā* (or *sakṛdvāsa*), blending them with water and grinding them until extremely fine. Then, add milk and boil them together, subsequently adding cane sugar and honey. Once cooled, it should be administered.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; if the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, if a woman’s pregnancy becomes unstable during the seventh month, one should take the branches, leaves, and roots of the *kaṇṭakārikā* (thorny plant), pound them into a fine powder, form them into pills with lactose and honey, and administer them with meat broth.
Furthermore, one may eat rice with meat broth, or consume green bean porridge and rice;
these medicines and meals can stabilize the womb, so that the patient, by taking them, attains peace and comfort.

"Furthermore, if a woman’s fetus becomes unstable during the eighth month of pregnancy, one should take equal parts of *trimaṅga* medicine, lotus, blue *utpala* flower, and thorn-apple (*kaṇṭakārikā*), grind them together with cold water until they are extremely fine, then add milk and sugar syrup, boil them together, and once cooled, administer it for consumption."
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; if the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, if a woman carrying a fetus reaches the ninth month and the womb becomes unstable, one should take equal parts of *śyāmāka* root, *kākodumbarikā*, *śarapāṇḍu*, and *mṛdvīkā* drugs, mix them with cold water, grind them until extremely fine, add breast milk, and boil them together. Once cooled, this should be administered.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; if the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, for a woman whose fetus becomes unstable in the tenth month of pregnancy, one should take equal parts of mung beans and *utpala* flowers, blend them with water and grind them until extremely fine. Then, add cane sugar, honey, and breast milk, and boil them together. Once cooled, the mixture should be consumed.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; when the patient takes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, for a woman whose pregnancy extends beyond eleven months and whose womb is unstable, one should take equal parts of blue utpala flowers, śaluka root, and lotus roots with their stalks, grind them together with cold water until extremely fine, then add milk and sugar to boil together. Once cooled, she should drink it.
This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; when the patient consumes it, they will attain peace and comfort.

Furthermore, for a woman whose pregnancy extends to the twelfth month and whose womb is unstable, one should take equal parts of *kākolī*, *kṣīrakākolī*, licorice (*yaṣṭimadhu*), and blue lotus (*utpala*). Grind and sift them until fine, then grind them together with water. Subsequently, add milk, blend thoroughly, and boil until cooked. Allow it to cool before consuming it.
"This medicine can stabilize the womb and alleviate pain; if the patient takes it, they will attain peace and well-being.
At that time, having heard the seer Jīvaka explain this method for nurturing a pregnant woman, he received it with joy and faith, paid his respects, and withdrew.
The Scripture on the Rishi Kāśyapa’s Discourse on Healing Women, Spoken by the Rishi Kāśyapa.
